challenge.better_approach: Considered matching against git grep -w: -w treats '.' and '/' as non-word, so 'superclaude.py' still matches 'superclaude' — wrong. A right-boundary regex in namers() is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a path followed by '.' is always a sibling: a target 'a/b' named as 'a/b.' at a sentence end would be missed. The boundary must treat '.' followed by a non-identifier (or end) as a boundary, so prose 'see a/b.' still counts.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons tickets naming machines/retire for prefix/needle/sibling and questions for retire+needle: none. retire's own charter (ticket 750ead1af9c1) and proof test_retire_checks_callers_in_the_act.py fixture only targets without siblings.
challenge.real_collision: None with retire's charter: its why (delete after measuring nobody calls it) is served better by fewer false callers; false namers only cost time and make it stricter, never unsafe, so this is efficiency + report accuracy, a distinction to record.

answers.falsifier: a target whose only textual neighbour is a sibling with the target's name as prefix yields zero namers; a file naming the target exactly is still a namer; e179's bash superclaude retires with namers limited to files that name the bash itself
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: retire's namers over cairn/devices/cc/superclaude returned 18 files, all naming the sibling superclaude.py, in wt-e179 (log ~/.akien/temp/cc0-pending-2026-11-23/e179_retire.log, rc=124 after 3000s)
answers.how: needles() stays; namers() matches each needle with a boundary on its right (not followed by a path/identifier character such as [A-Za-z0-9_.-] then an identifier char); red-first proof in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/retire/proofs adds a scratch repo where a target `tool` sits beside `tool.py` and only a file naming `tool.py` exists, asserting namers() is empty, and a file naming `tool` itself still counts.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (the door re-ran 47 proofs twice to re-derive that nothing calls a file nothing names) and Law 3 (its caller report names false callers, so the measurement is wrong)
answers.what: CodeMother's retire counts a file as naming a target only when the target's path or dotted module appears as a whole name, not as the prefix of a sibling's (superclaude must not match superclaude.py or cairn.devices.cc.superclaude_x).

bullets.text: retire's needle is a bare substring, so retiring X beside X.py runs every proof of everything naming X.py — e179's bash superclaude retire ran >50 min and timed out
